objectives.title: See what's in the workspace before you start
objectives.why: Knowing what pages, teams and people already exist avoids creating a duplicate of something that's already there.

objectives.title: Create a page directly from your agent
objectives.why: Writing it down where the team already looks beats a note that only lives in your chat history.

objectives.title: Keep an existing page current instead of leaving it stale
objectives.why: A page nobody updates becomes a page nobody trusts, and then nobody reads.

objectives.title: Keep the workspace organized by moving pages to where they belong
objectives.why: A page under the wrong parent is a page nobody else will ever find again.

objectives.title: Duplicate a page instead of rebuilding it from scratch
objectives.why: Starting from a working template beats re-creating its structure by hand every time.

objectives.title: Structure information as a database instead of a loose page
objectives.why: A database gives you filters, views and properties a wall of text never will.

objectives.title: Evolve a database's schema as requirements change
objectives.why: Updating properties as needs change beats working around a schema that no longer fits.

objectives.title: Build the right view for the audience, not just the default table
objectives.why: A board for the team standup and a calendar for deadlines both beat forcing everyone through one raw table.

objectives.title: Query your data instead of scrolling to find it
objectives.why: A structured query answers the question directly; scrolling a database just delays finding out you were looking in the wrong place.

objectives.title: Search your own meeting notes instead of trying to remember what was said
objectives.why: The notes already have the answer; memory is the unreliable fallback, not the first move.

objectives.title: Leave feedback where the work actually is
objectives.why: A comment on the page survives; the same feedback in a DM gets lost the moment the thread scrolls.

bestPractices.title: Don't hardcode Notion page/database IDs or integration tokens in source
bestPractices.why: An integration token committed to the repo is workspace access for anyone who can read the repo, including forks.

criteria.rubric: Does the code read Notion integration tokens and database/page IDs from environment variables or config, rather than hardcoding them as string literals?

bestPractices.title: Require confirmation before an agent moves, duplicates, or bulk-edits pages
bestPractices.why: notion-move-pages and notion-update-page act on a real, shared workspace other people may be looking at right now — an unreviewed bulk move is not like an unreviewed local file edit.

criteria.rubric: Do the project rules require explicit human confirmation before an agent moves, duplicates, or bulk-modifies pages in the Notion workspace?
